description: Loans and cards taken out without her knowledge, or signed under threat or manipulation; coercive use of authorised-user status; being made to write a bad cheque or file a fraudulent return.
energy_note: Her name, his spending, her credit file.

aspect: It does not require overt threat
description: It can be produced indirectly - framing the debt as proof of loyalty, or promising repayment with no intention of repaying. A victim may also know coercion is occurring and judge it safer not to challenge it.
energy_note: Knowing exactly what it is, and it being safer to sign.

aspect: The consequences are structural and long
description: 46% of surveyed survivors reported credit damage directly resulting from a partner's actions, and those subjected to coerced debt faced a sixfold higher likelihood of credit denial - impairing housing, loans and jobs with background checks.
energy_note: Six times more likely to be refused, for years after he has gone.

aspect: VILLAIN SCENE - the paperwork on the counter
description: 'It's just the consolidation thing, saves us about eighty a month.' She signs. It is not a consolidation. She finds out fourteen months later, from a letter, after he has left.
energy_note: Signed in four seconds, discovered in fourteen months.
